findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so archived reports are stored without an explicitly enforced encryption-at-rest policy and are not protected by the customer-managed KMS key used elsewhere in this configuration.
The ledger_exports bucket holds financial ledger exports but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving this sensitive data without an explicitly configured encryption-at-rest policy.
The model_artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so proprietary model artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

The ops_runbooks bucket stores operational runbooks, which commonly contain internal procedures and credentials, but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so contents are not covered by an enforced encryption-at-rest policy.

The audit_trail bucket is configured with acl = "log-delivery-write", which grants the S3 log delivery group write access and read-ACP permission on a bucket containing tamper-sensitive audit logs; the ACL is broader than required and allows log-delivery principals to alter bucket ACLs.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the reports bucket and no acl is specified, so there is no account- or bucket-level guardrail (block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, restrict_public_buckets) preventing the bucket from being made public by a future ACL or policy change.
The model_artifacts bucket relies only on acl = "private" with no public access block resource, so it can be made public through a future ACL or bucket policy change without a guardrail.
The ops_runbooks bucket sets acl = "private" but has no accompanying public access block, so it can be made public by a later policy or ACL change without an account- or bucket-level safeguard.
The audit_trail bucket has no public access block and carries a non-private canned ACL, leaving audit logs without a guardrail against later permissive policy or ACL changes.

The reports_archive bucket differs from the other buckets in this configuration by not enabling access logging via a logging block, so access to archived reports is not recorded and cannot be audited.
